Thank you for raising these concerns, and thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond here. Getting a letter from a law firm after asking for help is frightening, and we take that seriously.

Here is how our clinic handles attendee information. Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing attendee information. Landlords and their attorneys are specifically excluded from receiving it. Sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage and are not provided to outside parties.

Eviction filings in magistrate court are public records, and some law firms use them to send mailings to tenants. That is the most likely explanation for the letters people have described, though we understand that doesn't make the timing any less upsetting. We can't speak to any individual's situation here, and we ask everyone to avoid posting personal details in this thread, for the privacy of all neighbors.

We understand the frustration, and we are not upset with anyone for asking questions. You should be able to ask them, and we would rather answer them directly.

The library meeting room is unavailable on Saturday, November 14, so the clinic has moved to Mt Zion Fellowship Hall in East Atlanta. The hours are the same, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Please use the side entrance by the parking lot, which is accessible.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, and everyone is welcome. It's walk-in, no appointment needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

Questions can go to clinic@cascaderights.example, or you can call our office at 404-555-0187.
